title: AI CREATIVITY — CLP Part 1 - AI & Creativity Workshop
notes: Welcome to the Camden Community Leadership Programme AI & Creativity Workshop (Part 1).

title: You don't need permission from gatekeepers to tell your story — AI gives your community's
notes: Welcome everyone to the Community Leadership Programme AI workshop. Today is about one thing: Creative Self-Determination. You are running vital community charities across Camden—often completely solo, juggling families, jobs, and sleepless nights. AI isn't here to replace you; it's here to give you an extra pair of hands so your community's authentic voice can never be ignored.

title: AI & Creative Self-Determination
notes: That is what we call Creative Self-Determination. It’s not about cutting headcount or corporate efficiency—it’s about giving you the agency and confidence to tell your community’s story on your own terms, without waiting for permission or big budgets.

section: II. Grant Writing — Camden Giving & Gemini
title: The #1 Founder Bottleneck — You voted Grant Writing as your biggest headache.
notes: Right—we have looked at the weird, delightful things we make at Creative Lab. Now let’s get practical, starting with the #1 operational bottleneck you voted for in Oliver’s survey: Grant Writing. Sitting in front of a blank screen at 11 PM trying to guess what corporate jargon funders want to hear. Today, we turn Gemini into your 24/7 personal grant strategist.

notes: This isn't a theoretical exercise. Our program partner, Camden Giving, has The Equality Fund 2026 open right now. It closes on October 17th at midday—two weeks from today. Every single charity in this room is eligible to apply for up to £20,000.

section: II. Grant Writing — Camden Giving & Gemini
title: Not corporate bureaucrats or bank trustees. — A panel of local Camden citizens with lived
notes: Here's the secret: Camden Giving uses participatory grantmaking. Your application is not read by corporate bureaucrats or bank trustees—it is read and decided by a panel of local Camden citizens who have personal lived experience of inequality. When a neighbour from Somers Town or Kilburn reads your proposal, they can smell corporate buzzwords and AI slop a mile away. They want the honest truth of your street.

section: II. Grant Writing — Camden Giving & Gemini
title: NOT THIS — Corporate AI Slop
notes: If you wouldn't say it sitting across a kitchen table over a cup of tea, don't let AI write it. Corporate jargon gets rejected by local panels. Grounded street reality wins.

section: II. Grant Writing — Camden Giving & Gemini
title: Gemini knows the world. — Personal Intelligence connects it to YOUR charity's Docs & Drive
notes: Right now, most AI is like a stranger on the street—it knows the internet, but nothing about your charity. Personal Intelligence bridges that gap by securely connecting Gemini to your Google Workspace—your Docs, Drive, and Gmail. Instead of digging through folders for last year's impact numbers or trustee notes, Gemini can pull straight from your own documents.

section: II. Grant Writing — Camden Giving & Gemini
title: Gems — Gems = Who you talk to, a specialist who remembers your rules.
notes: The biggest time-waster in AI is prompt fatigue—re-explaining what your charity does, who you serve in Camden, and your Kitchen Table tone in every new chat. Gemini Gems fix that. A Gem is a custom specialist you set up once with your charity's background and Camden Giving's rules. Whenever a new grant opens, you just open your Grant Partner Gem and start talking.

section: II. Grant Writing — Camden Giving & Gemini
title: Skills — Skills = Playbooks you trigger, modular actions you run on any draft.
notes: If a Gem is a specialist you chat with, Skills are modular playbooks you can trigger at any moment. Today we are going to use 1 Gem to interview us and write our first draft, and then trigger 2 custom Skills—tough-evaluator and peer-scorecard—to stress-test our facts and cross out any corporate buzzwords.

title: AI is not a creative genius. — It's a fast, obedient, slightly naive pair of hands.
notes: Welcome back! You now have a grounded grant draft for your charity. Next, let’s give your project a visual voice to match—without a £20,000 corporate agency on retainer. When it comes to visuals, AI isn’t here to replace your taste; it’s a fast, obedient pair of hands. You are the editor-in-chief.

title: Default AI: Oily plastic, exaggerated tears, pity-mongering. — Authentic Craft: Physical t
notes: You've all seen AI slop. It's that glossy, airbrushed, video-game sheen. When people type 'homeless charity poster', the machine draws crying children in dark alleys with neon lens flares. It feels exploitative and fake. In community work, trust is everything. If your flyer looks like an energy drink advert, nobody trusts you. Dignity is non-negotiable.

notes: Infuse everything with your soul. People love to connect with people, they are not impressed by polished posters.

title: 3 colors, 2 seconds, looping. 100 gifs — REPETITION IS STYLE
notes: Repetition is style. When you lock in strict rules—3 colors, 2-second loops, one consistent texture—suddenly 100 different clips feel like a unified brand campaign. For your charity, picking one visual rule and repeating it everywhere builds instant recognition across Camden.

title: MY ADVICE — 1. [Write a 1 sentence style]
notes: Stop writing long, polite paragraphs to image tools. Use this two-part formula: first, lock in your visual style in three beats—a one-sentence style, a physical medium with limited colours, and real physical imperfections like ink bleed or paper grain. Then, and only then, write one sentence describing your subject. And ban the word 'photorealistic'—that word triggers the computer's cheesy 3D rendering engine and guarantees plastic slop.

title: STYLE 1 — Risograph
notes: Style Card 1: Risograph. Inspired by independent community printshops across London. Strictly two inks—high-contrast scarlet red and deep blue. You get visible halftone dots, grain dithering, and subtle ink misregistration. It feels tactile, joyful, and handmade.

section: IV. Layout in Google Slides & Sprint
title: Don't Let AI Spell! — AI is an illustrator, not a typesetter.
notes: Here is the golden rule: NEVER let AI write words on your poster. It will spell your charity's name wrong, pick terrible fonts, and crowd the frame. Treat AI purely as your background illustrator. Add your typography in Google Slides where you have 100% control.

section: IV. Layout in Google Slides & Sprint
title: Negative Space — Always direct empty space for your text.
notes: Always instruct the AI where to leave empty space. Say: 'Subject framed in the bottom third, open wall in top third for text.' That gives you an instant clean billboard ready for your headline, date, and QR code.
